Goal: one pull request that lets packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js lint several files at once and read stdin via -, with tests and README, closing issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104.

Acceptance lines (all must hold):
1. packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before
2. A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)
3. Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)
4. lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged
5. node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage
6. The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head

Steps:
1. Read packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.
2. Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all (git diff on it must be empty).
3. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js:
   - Take all of process.argv.slice(2) as file names. No arguments: usage message on stderr (e.g. `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`), exit 2, nothing on stdout.
   - If - appears more than once: usage error on stderr, exit 2. Do this check before reading anything (stdin can only be read once), and print nothing on stdout.
   - For each name in the order given: read `-` from stdin (readFileSync(0, 'utf8') is fine), else readFileSync(name, 'utf8'). If a read fails, write `jsonl-lint: cannot read <name>: <message>` to stderr, remember the failure, and carry on with the next file.
   - For each file read, run lint(text) and print `<name>:<line>: <error>` per problem exactly as the single-file code does now (same newline-flattening of the error), using the argument exactly as given (`-` for stdin).
   - Exit 2 if any file couldn't be read, else 1 if any problem was found in any file, else 0. (2 takes priority over 1 when both happen.)
   - Keep single-file behaviour byte-for-byte the same as before so existing tests still pass.
4. Add node:test tests to packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (spawnSync with `input` for stdin), each asserting exit status and stdout/stderr:
   - two clean files → exit 0, empty stdout;
   - one bad file among several clean ones → exit 1, only that file's rows printed with its name prefix, in order;
   - stdin via - clean → exit 0; stdin via - bad → exit 1, lines prefixed `-:`;
   - a missing file among good ones (put a bad file after the missing one too, or at least a good one after it) → exit 2, stderr names the missing file, other files still checked/reported;
   - two - arguments → exit 2, usage error on stderr;
   - no arguments → exit 2, usage on stderr.
   Also a test that multiple files are reported in argument order is worthwhile.
5. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: usage line `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`, explain `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-` (only once), and update the exit codes section (0 all clean, 1 any bad row, 2 no file / unreadable file / second `-`, other files still checked).
6. Run `npm test` at the repo root; all must pass.
7. Commit, push, and open one PR against suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow on the PR head to finish and be green; fix and push again if not.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 at its head commit. Check out the head, run `npm ci` at the repo root, and use a scratch temp directory for fixture files. One check per expect line, in order. Report PASS or FAIL for each with the evidence (commands and output).

Check 1 — "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before"
Run: create a.jsonl with content `{bad}\n{"x":1}\n` , b.jsonl with `{"ok":1}\n`, c.jsonl with `{"y":2}\n\n{oops\n`. Run `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js a.jsonl b.jsonl c.jsonl` and also each file alone (`node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js a.jsonl` etc.).
PASS: the multi-file stdout contains `a.jsonl:1: <error>` then `c.jsonl:3: <error>`, in that order (a's lines before c's), nothing for b, and each line matches what the single-file run of that file prints. Also reversing the argument order (c.jsonl b.jsonl a.jsonl) puts c's lines first.
FAIL: any file's bad rows are missing, files are reported out of argument order, the format is not `<file>:<line>: <error>`, or lines differ from the single-file output.

Check 2 — "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)"
Run: `printf '{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js -`; `printf '{"a":1}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js b.jsonl -`; `printf '{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js - b.jsonl -; echo $?`.
PASS: the first prints a line starting `-:1: `; the second reports nothing for the clean stdin; the third exits 2.
FAIL: stdin is not read for -, it is reported under another name than -, or two - arguments do not exit 2.

Check 3 — "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)"
Run and record exit status, stdout, stderr for: `jsonl-lint.js b.jsonl b.jsonl` (all clean); `jsonl-lint.js b.jsonl a.jsonl b.jsonl` (one bad); `jsonl-lint.js` (no args); `jsonl-lint.js b.jsonl missing.jsonl c.jsonl` (missing among others, c bad).
PASS: exits are 0, 1, 2, 2 respectively; for the missing-file run stderr has an error message and stdout still has c.jsonl's bad-row line(s) (c was still checked); for no args there is a message on stderr.
FAIL: any exit code differs, the read error is not on stderr, or files after the unreadable one are not checked/reported.

Check 4 — "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged"
Run: `git diff <merge-base with main>..HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` (find the merge base with `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`), and run `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js`.
PASS: the lint function in packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js is unchanged by the PR (no diff to it).
FAIL: the PR changes the lint function.

Check 5 — "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage"
Run: `npm test -w packages/jsonl-lint` (or `node --test` in packages/jsonl-lint) and read the test files under packages/jsonl-lint/test/ and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md at the head.
PASS: there are node:test tests (run and passing) that exercise each of: two clean files; one bad file among several; stdin via - clean; stdin via - bad; a missing file among good ones; two - arguments; no arguments. The README documents the multi-file usage (more than one file and the - stdin argument).
FAIL: any of these seven cases has no test, the tests are not node:test, or the README does not document the usage.

Check 6 — "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run: `gh pr view <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid,state`; `gh pr checks <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test`; `npm test` at the repo root at the head.
PASS: the PR is on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test, its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, the `test` workflow check for the head commit succeeded, and `npm test` locally passes.
FAIL: the body lacks that text, the test workflow at the head failed or is not complete/green, or npm test fails.

Advisory (not pass/fail):
- When a file is unreadable and another file has bad rows, exit 2 is expected to take priority over 1.
- Check that with two - arguments nothing is printed on stdout and stdin is not consumed before the error.
- Stderr message wording is not fixed by the issue.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #104, and the harness accepted them. I didn't change, commit or push anything in the repo.

**Builder brief.** It asks for one PR that makes `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` accept several files and read `-` from stdin:
- **Order and format:** files are checked in the order given. Each bad row prints exactly as the single-file version does now.
- **Errors:** a second `-` is a usage error, checked before anything is read. A file that can't be read is reported on stderr and the remaining files are still checked.
- **Exit codes:** 2 if any file can't be read, otherwise 1 if any row is bad, otherwise 0.
- **Unchanged:** `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` must not be touched.
- **Tests and README:** node:test tests for the seven cases the issue lists, and README updates for usage, `-` and exit codes.
- **PR:** the body must say `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, and the builder waits for the `test` workflow to pass.

**Verifier brief.** It has six checks, one per expect line and in the same order. Each one runs something at the PR head: the CLI on temporary fixture files and piped stdin, a `git diff` on `src/index.js` against the merge base, the package tests, `gh pr view` / `gh pr checks`, and `npm test` at the root.

One thing the issue doesn't settle: what the exit code should be when one file can't be read and another has bad rows. The builder brief says 2 wins. In the verifier brief that rule only appears under Advisory, not in a PASS/FAIL condition, so the expect lines don't decide it. The same goes for the exact stderr wording and for printing nothing on stdout when `-` is given twice.
